name: Emdash
description: Open-source desktop app for running multiple coding agents in parallel with isolated worktrees. Provider-agnostic platform supporting 28+ coding agent providers with SSH support for remote machines, diff review, and PR shipping.
community_quotes: One app, every coding agent. Emdash is a provider-agnostic desktop app to run agents in parallel and turn issues into PRs
Parallel agents with isolated worktrees is the part that catches my eye
Been using Emdash for the past week and its great
Closing the development flow in app is the right call
This is literally that one feature which will make me switch from Cursor

name: Runtime
description: Sandboxed coding agents platform for teams. Provides isolated environments for running AI coding agents with team collaboration features via Slack integration.
community_quotes: Sandboxed coding agents for everyone on your team

name: Re_gent
description: Version control system for AI agent activity. Shows what coding agents changed, which prompts caused changes, and enables rollback across files and sessions. Git for AI agents.
community_quotes: Shows what your agent did and which prompt wrote each line of code

name: Glia
description: Local-first AI memory bridge between browser chats and IDEs. Chrome extension that auto-saves web-based Claude/ChatGPT conversations and serves them via MCP to IDEs for persistent context.
community_quotes: Local-first AI memory bridge between browser chats and IDEs

name: Contextberg
description: Local memory app for AI agents that watches screens, browser history, and agent conversations in the background, serving context to coding agents via MCP protocol.
community_quotes: Turn your work into AI agent memory, served over MCP
Local memory app for AI agents
